# Four common-vertex triangle fibers: the remaining peak case

Let \(T=\operatorname{conv}(0,e_1,e_2)\), \(V=|T|\), and \(\Gamma=4/9\).
Suppose the actual integer fibers at bases \(0,1,2,3\) are \(r_kT\),
where the four radii are positive and concave. Then an own-fiber centroid
has every closed containing ambient halfspace of mass at least
\[
 \frac29V\sum_{k=0}^3r_k^2.                                      \tag{1}
\]
The monotone cases are proved in
four-monotone-triangle-fibers-own-centroid-theorem.md.
This note proves all remaining profiles, including repeated maxima.
A common invertible continuous linear change and an affine common-vertex
shear preserve the result. Section 7 uses the independently proved
centroid comparison to extend the conclusion to arbitrary compatible
translations of four positively homothetic triangles.

After reversing the integer base and scaling by its largest radius, a
remaining profile has form
\[
 (a,b,1,c),\qquad0<a\le2b-1,\quad\tfrac12<b\le1,\quad0<c\le1.       \tag{2}
\]
Indeed the first concavity inequality is \(a\le2b-1\); the other one is
automatic because \(c\le1\le2-b\). Put \(S=a^2+b^2+1+c^2\).
If \(S\le2\), the largest fiber's own centroid already proves (1).
We establish, without any heavy-fiber assumption, the following explicit
all-cap bounds at the two actual middle own centroids:
\[
\begin{split}
 y_1&=(1,b/3,b/3),&\operatorname{depth}(y_1)/V
    &\ge L_1:=\frac{4b^2+7a^2}{9},\\
 y_2&=(2,1/3,1/3),&\operatorname{depth}(y_2)/V
    &\ge L_2:=\frac{4+7h^2}{9},\\
 h&=\left[\min(b,c)-\frac43(1-\max(b,c))\right]_+ .
\end{split}                                                     \tag{3}
\]
We then prove the exact scalar inequality
\[
 \max(L_1,L_2)\ge\frac29S.                                       \tag{4}
\]
A deterministic rule is to use \(y_1\) if its displayed lower bound
reaches the target, and \(y_2\) otherwise.

## 1. The subset theorem used here

The proved theorem in
candidate 6c259b3f68b388b0 states:
if a triangle \(L\) has centroid zero and \(E\subset L\) is measurable
with area \(e\), then the three sources \(E,L,L\) at bases \(-1,0,1\)
satisfy
\[
 \operatorname{depth}(0,0)\ge\frac49|L|+\frac79e.                 \tag{5}
\]
This holds for all nonvertical directions, all shared base tilts,
closed vertical caps, and base reversal. It keeps one continuous normal
and opposing endpoint thresholds. The coefficient \(7/9\) is sharp even
for an actual compatible convex subset \(E\). It is not a sum of
independently minimized fiber profiles.

## 2. The first middle centroid

Set \(g=(1/3,1/3)\), \(K=T-g\), and retain bases \(0,1,2\).
In local coordinates \(z=k-1\), apply the permitted shear
\[
 x'=x-bg-z(1-b)g.                                               \tag{6}
\]
It preserves integer bases, all fiber areas, and the ambient halfspace
class. The fibers become
\[
 A'=aK+(a+1-2b)g,\qquad bK,\qquad K.
\]
With \(\delta=2b-1-a\ge0\) and \(-g\in K\), convexity gives
\[
 A'=aK-\delta g\subset(a+\delta)K=(2b-1)K\subset bK.              \tag{7}
\]
The right endpoint contains \(bK\). Apply (5) to the retained sources
\(A',bK,bK\), at the original centroid \(y_1\).
Since \(|A'|=a^2V\), this gives \(L_1\).
The unused fourth fiber and the unused endpoint portion add nonnegative
mass to every cap. Their centroids have not been identified.

## 3. The second middle centroid

Retain bases \(1,2,3\), reversing this triple if necessary so its radii
are \((r,1,s)\) at local bases \(-1,0,1\), with
\(r=\min(b,c)\le s=\max(b,c)\).
The shear
\[
 x'=x-g-z(s-1)g
\]
transforms the fibers to
\[
 A'=rK+(r+s-2)g,\qquad K,\qquad sK.                            \tag{8}
\]
Translate \(A'\) and \(sK\) by \(sg\). They become
\[
 rT-\eta(1,1),\qquad sT,\qquad \eta=\tfrac23(1-s)\ge0.
\]
Their intersection has nonnegative coordinates and coordinate sum at
most \(r-2\eta\); the bound \(s\) is redundant since \(r-2\eta\le r\le s\).
Consequently its area is exactly \(h^2V\), with \(h\) from (3), when
\(h>0\); for a nonpositive unclipped expression use the empty set.
For positive \(h\) an exact retained subset is
\[
 E=hT-sg\subset A'\cap sK.                                    \tag{9}
\]
Apply (5) to \(E,sK,sK\), retaining the central \(sK\) inside \(K\).
For every nonvertical through-cap the extra actual middle mass is
\[
 |K\cap\{ux'\ge0\}|-|sK\cap\{ux'\ge0\}|
   =(1-s^2)|K\cap\{ux'\ge0\}|
   \ge\frac49(1-s^2)V.                                      \tag{10}
\]
The two middle bodies have the same centroid, essential for this
identity. Adding (10) to (5) proves \(L_2\).
A closed vertical through-cap has mass at least \((1+r^2)V\), exceeding
\(L_2V\) since \(h\le r\). Every containing cap contains a parallel
through-cap. Hence both bounds in (3) include all original halfspaces.

## 4. Scalar closure for \(c\ge b\)

The actual target is at most
\[
 T_1=\frac29[1+b^2+c^2+(2b-1)^2].
\]
We prove the stronger inequality
\[
 \frac49+\frac12h^2\ge T_1.                                   \tag{11}
\]
If \(h>0\), put \(v=c-b\ge0\). The difference in (11) is
\[
 Q=\frac{(5b-4)^2}{18}
      +\left(\frac83b-\frac{16}{9}\right)v+\frac23v^2.          \tag{12}
\]
For \(b\ge2/3\) all terms are nonnegative.
For \(1/2\le b\le2/3\), completing the square gives
\[
 Q\ge-\frac{69b^2-72b+16}{54}>0.
\]
The numerator is convex and has endpoint values \(-11/4,-4/3\).
If \(h=0\), then \(b\le4/7\) and \(c\le1-3b/4\), so
\[
 \frac49-T_1\ge
 \frac29\left[\frac{11}{2}b-\frac{89}{16}b^2-1\right]>0.        \tag{13}
\]
The bracket is concave on \([1/2,4/7]\), with endpoint values
\(23/64,16/49\). This proves (11), hence (4), in this case.

## 5. Scalar closure for \(c\le b\)

If \(L_1\) misses the target, then
\[
 a^2<\frac25(1+c^2-b^2).                                     \tag{14}
\]
Combining this with \(a^2\le(2b-1)^2\), the target is at most
\[
 \min(T_1,T_2),\qquad T_2=\frac{14(1+c^2)+6b^2}{45}.           \tag{15}
\]
The comparison with \(T_2\) is strict under (14).
It suffices to prove at least one of
\[
\begin{split}
 7h^2&\ge R_1:=10b^2-8b+2c^2,\\
 35h^2&\ge R_2:=14c^2+6b^2-6,
\end{split}                                                   \tag{16}
\]
which are exactly \(L_2\ge T_1\) and \(L_2\ge T_2\).

For \(h>0\), set \(e=1-b\), so \(c=h+4e/3\) and \(0\le e<3/7\).
Direct expansion gives
\[
\begin{split}
 9(7h^2-R_1)
   &=45h^2-48eh-122e^2+108e-18=:D_1,\\
 9(35h^2-R_2)
   &=189h^2-336eh-278e^2+108e=:D_2.
\end{split}                                                   \tag{17}
\]
For \(0\le e\le1/4\),
\[
 D_2=189(h-\tfrac89e)^2+
       e(108-\tfrac{1282}{3}e)\ge0,                           \tag{18}
\]
because the bracket is at least \(7/6\).
For \(1/4\le e\le3/7\),
\[
 D_1=45(h-\tfrac8{15}e)^2+
       108e-\tfrac{674}{5}e^2-18>0.                          \tag{19}
\]
The last quadratic is concave and has positive endpoint values
\(23/40,864/245\). These completed squares were independently derived
by the parent audit and checked here. They prove (16) for positive \(h\).

For \(h=0\), one has \(c\le4e/3\).
If \(b\le2/3\), then \(R_1\le12b^2-8b\le0\).
If \(2/3\le b\le3/4\), then \(1/4\le e\le1/3\), and
\[
 -9R_1\ge108e-18-122e^2>0.
\]
This concave quadratic has endpoint values \(11/8,40/9\).
If \(b\ge3/4\), then \(0\le e\le1/4\), and
\[
 -9R_2\ge108e-278e^2\ge0.
\]
Thus (16) holds also for zero \(h\), proving (4).

## 6. Body completion and exact scope

The piecewise linear roof \(r(z)\) through the four radii is concave.
Thus
\[
 C=\{0\le z\le3,\ x_1,x_2\ge0,\ x_1+x_2\le r(z)\}
\]
is a compact full-dimensional convex body, is the convex hull of its
four lifted triangles, and has exactly the prescribed integer fibers.
Every shear used above preserves the integer coordinate and continuous
area. The chosen points pull back to the original own centroids.
All unused original mass remains present when a cap is evaluated.

Every positive concave four-term sequence is either monotone or, after
reversal, has form (2). Combining this note with the monotone theorem
proves (1) for all four common-vertex triangle chains. The exact verifier
is verify_four_triangle_peak_centroids.py.
The earlier exploratory independent-envelope failures are not used.

## 7. Arbitrary compatible translations

Let an actual mixed source in one integer and two continuous dimensions
have exactly four positive-area fibers, all positively homothetic to
one nondegenerate triangle \(K\) with centroid zero:
\[
 K_j=c_j+r_jK,\qquad r_j>0.
\]
The four positive bases are consecutive: Minkowski interpolation of
two positive-area fibers forces every intermediate integer fiber to
have positive area. Translate the integer coordinate so they are
\(0,1,2,3\). Any other zero-area fibers carry no mixed mass.

Actual convex compatibility and planar Brunn--Minkowski imply that
\((r_0,r_1,r_2,r_3)\) is concave. Fix a vertex \(v_0\) of \(K\) and
form the reference fibers \(r_j(K-v_0)\), all with common vertex zero.
Section 4 of the independently audited
candidate 24467ade6f021ae8
proves, at EACH specified own centroid, the exact comparison
\[
 \operatorname{depth}_{\rm original}(j,c_j)
  \ge \operatorname{depth}_{\rm reference}(j,-r_jv_0).          \tag{20}
\]
For clarity, the hypotheses required there all hold here: the common
centered shape is a full-dimensional simplex; scales are positive;
all finite anchored Minkowski inclusions follow from the actual convex
body; and the total masses of both families are exactly
\(|K|\sum r_j^2\). Its proof uses a finite affine support minorant at
the chosen base and a volume-preserving vertex permutation of the
centered simplex. Although that comparison map can depend on the
original cap and anchor, the reference family and its target centroid
in (20) are fixed. Vertical cap masses agree exactly, so no boundary
fiber is lost.

The reference triangle is linearly equivalent to \(T\), and every
fiber area scales by the same determinant. Apply the monotone theorem
or the peak theorem proved above to choose a reference own centroid
with absolute depth at least \(2M/9\). Equation (20) transfers the
same lower bound to the corresponding ORIGINAL own centroid.
Therefore every actual four-fiber family of positively homothetic
triangles, with arbitrary compatible translations, satisfies the
required \(n=1,d=2\) bound.

This also gives the statement for at most four positive homothetic
triangle fibers: one or two fibers have a half-mass heavy fiber, and
the three-fiber case follows from
three-homothetic-fibers-all-ratios-and-translations.md.
No arbitrary-length or nonhomothetic-triangle theorem is asserted.
